title: The Stranger's Chair
concept: An old man reserves a seat for his 'friend' at a crowded temple — everyone assumes it's for a VIP. The reveal: the friend never existed, but the wait was real.
narration: Mandir bhara hua tha. Aarti ki jyot lakh lakh haathon mein jal rahi thi. Magar ek kursi khali thi. Us par — ek purana, geela shawl. Tahta hua. Jaise kisi ne abhi-abhi uthaya ho. Log phusphusaye: "Kaun hai? Koi mantri? Koi baba?" Dadaji muskuraye. Haath shawl pe rakha. "Mera dost hai. Bas yeh seat chahiye." Ek ladki baith gayi us par. Dadaji ne usay uthaya. Shawl saaf kiya. "Abhi nahi." Ghanti baji. Aarti khatam. Bheed chhant gayi. Kursi khali. Shawl khali. Koi nahi aaya. Raat ko Dadaji ne wo shawl uthaya. Chooma. Bag mein rakh diya. Aur yaad aaya — pachpan saal pehle. Chhota Dadaji. Maa ki ungli pakde. Darwaze par. "Baba fauj mein hain, beta. Tuesday aayenge." Aaj bhi Tuesday hai. Woh aaye. Shawl mein. Seat mein. Intezaar mein. Har Tuesday.
